Olga / Marissa — summary from Privacy Counsel (high level):

Critical (we should push back / propose alternative):
- Subprocessors: DataWorks requests unrestricted right to engage subprocessors with only notification. Counsel recommends: 30-day notice + right to object in writing for specific processing of regulated data; automatic approval if we don't respond within 15 business days is acceptable. Proposed language in comments.
- EU transfers: DataWorks' redline wants controller-to-controller language. Counsel: must preserve processor obligations and standard contractual clauses (SCCs) or EU-US Addendum as fallback. Recommend we accept SCCs + offer an EU Addendum template; push back on controller-to-controller language.
- Audit & security evidence: DataWorks is asking for on-site audits and full scope logs. Counsel recommends scoped right to review SOC2 report + quarterly security summaries; offer customer-specific audit rights only for programmatic evidence requests, not full on-site audits unless minimum material incident.

Negotiable / middle ground:
- Liability cap: DataWorks asks for no cap for breach of confidentiality. Counsel suggests carve for intentional misconduct/regulatory fines only; keep standard cap at subscription fees x12 except for gross negligence.
- Data retention / deletion: propose specific retention schedule + data export window (30 days) — acceptable to most customers.

Minor / Acceptable:
- Standard definitions and notice clauses — no change.

Action items / next steps:
1) I attached counsel's annotated notes for the redline (RDW_privacy_counsel_notes.pdf). Please review our alternative language for subprocessors and transfers — see pages 3–5.
2) If Sales agrees, we can present a tracked-change counter with highlighted "must-haves" vs "concessions" and request DataWorks to accept.
3) After agreement, Legal Ops will prepare DocuSign packet and route to both signatories. Suggest we keep e-sign route open with a single exception appendix for the liability carve they requested.

Risks: If we concede to controller-to-controller, it sets a precedent for controller customers and weakens our processor commitments. Recommend explicit no-go on that point.
